title: Congress protests at Bengaluru petrol pumps over alleged excess ethanol blending

tea.why: Protesters alleged that petrol sold at fuel stations contains unauthorized levels of ethanol exceeding the prescribed 20 per cent limit.
tea.want: Demanding the Centre immediately suspend the ethanol blending programme, supply unblended fuel, and investigate the issue.
tea.changed: Nov 9: Congress workers staged demonstrations at multiple petrol bunks across Bengaluru, displaying posters and warning consumers.

summary: On November 9, 2026, Congress workers staged demonstrations at multiple petrol pumps across Bengaluru, including locations at Nehru Circle and in front of Mantri Mall in Malleswaram. Organised by the party, the protests targeted the alleged excessive blending of ethanol in petrol, which they termed 'E420' as a form of deception. Protesters displayed posters and sought to alert motorists about damage to vehicle engines and decreased mileage. They claimed laboratory tests commissioned by the Karnataka government showed ethanol content ranging from 21 to over 35 per cent, surpassing the prescribed 20 per cent limit. The party demanded that the Union government immediately suspend the ethanol blending programme and supply unblended fuel. In response, public sector oil marketing companies and the Union Petroleum and Natural Gas Ministry rejected the Karnataka government's claims, while BJP MP Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraj Wadiyar accused the Congress of attempting to divert public attention from rising prices.

response: Oil marketing companies and the Union Ministry rejected the claims, stating fuel complies with standards and questioning the testing methods. BJP MP Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraj Wadiyar accused Congress of using the issue to distract from rising prices.
